allowed_scope.extent: Implement a live-process trajectory-capture composition modeled on the proven C5/monitor_host supervision pattern (SupervisionConfig, host_records, systemd --user supervised run loop). Assign identity/order/timestamps to captured events, persist them durably and restart-safe, detect anomalies, reconcile old/new observations across a supervised restart without loss, using only this operator's own existing local systemd --user supervision. No new external target, service, budget, or custody arrangement.

Any claim of external-observer replacement or retirement; alienintent-observer.service remains the governing independent observer.
Replanning the DAG beyond this single insertion, or implementing another node's scope.
architecture_constraints: Reuse the existing SupervisionConfig/host_records/systemd-supervision pattern from src/alienintent/composition/monitor_host.py rather than inventing a new supervision mechanism.

Preserve compatible interfaces, persisted resource identities, one-writer ownership. Changes to monitor_host.py or offline_proof.py that could regress C5 or WO-220101 must preserve their existing behavior.

owner_clarifications_disposed.anomaly_classes_and_response: Detect: sequence gaps, out-of-order events, duplicate identities, timestamp regressions, capture stalls. On detection: record a durable anomaly evidence record (append-only). Do not alert or halt.
owner_clarifications_disposed.restart_loss_boundary: Guarantee covers only already-accepted (durably recorded) events at the moment of restart — those must survive without loss or duplication. Events a live source might emit while the process is down are out of this node's scope (no buffered/replayable upstream source is built here).

dependencies.completion_predicate: Real temporary SQLite; disposable local bare Git remote, publication/fetch into a fresh verifier worktree, local work-management and provider transport, injected clock/IDs, durable scripted worker journal, credentials absent and enforced denied outbound network with attempted-network refusal.

Under existing SWF-27 / SF-REQ-053 ownership, independently supervise the monitor/scanner host. Terminate or stall monitor/scanner, observe external health detection/alert, and demonstrate authorized restart preserving generation and pending state.

required_evidence: Retain exact fixture/source/candidate revisions, invocation and command, expected/observed result, exit status, immutable observation refs.
Retain predecessor candidate identities and full command/exit status. Preserve prior proof on repair; supersession needs explicit authority.

criteria: Identity/order/timestamp assignment is stable and correct across a supervised kill/restart.
Every already-accepted event survives the restart without loss or duplication (per the disposed restart-loss boundary).
Each seeded anomaly class (sequence gap, out-of-order event, duplicate identity, timestamp regression, capture stall) produces a durable anomaly evidence record.
Captured events and anomaly records are durably persisted and readable after restart.
material_failure_classes: Identity/order/timestamp assignment is unstable, incorrect, or undefined across the restart.
An already-accepted event is lost or duplicated across the restart.
A seeded anomaly class is not detected, or detection is not recorded durably.
The composition invents a new external target, service, or upstream buffering contract beyond this operator's own local systemd --user supervision.
A change to monitor_host.py or offline_proof.py regresses C5's or WO-220101's own existing proof.
non_claims: No claim that this satisfies WO-220504/Issue #124's own separately authorized operational-target proof.
No claim of external-observer replacement or retirement.
No release, cutover, or broader production mutation is authorized.
